' A New Jersey man facing trial in the 197£ slay-
ing of his family is not the legendary airline
hijacker known as D.B. Cooper, a New Jersey
investigator said Monday. :

The FBI long ago concluded that Cooper most
likely died when he jumped from a Northwest
Airlines 727 over Southwest Washington with
$200,000 on Nov. 24, 1971. However, the agency has
continued to investigate tips it receives about
Cooper's true identity. Since June, agents have
been trying to determine whether John List, now
64, could be Cooper.

List vanished Nov. 9, 1971, the day authorities
think his mother, wife and tliree teen-age children
were shot to death in the family's home at West-
field, N.J. After investigators found the five bod-
ies Dec. 9, 1971, they considered the possibility
that List could be Cooper.

"There are no new
developments."

-— John Eyer,
FBI agent

The New Jersey man was not found until this
year. His arrest June 1 at Midlothian, Va., reacti-
vated the FBI's interest in him. .

However, Capt. Frank Marranca of the Union
County, N.J., prosecutor's office, said Monday in
a telephone interview, "The best we can deter-
mine, John List was in Denver" at the time of the
hijacking. '"'As far as we can tell he's not D.B.
Cooper."

Marranea said he could not discuss what led
authorities to conclude that List had been in
Colorado at the time of the hijacking because |

ist has not been tried on the murder charges.

John Eyer, assistant agent in charge of the FBI
office in Seaftle, said he could not comment on
Marranca's statement because the investigation
was pending. He said only, "There are no new
developments."

Ralph Himmelsbach, the retired FBI agent who
investigated the hijacking for nine years, sai
Marranca's statement was "very consistent wit
my belief" that Cooper perished in the 1971 jump
If Cooper had survived, he said, a number o
coincidences made the New Jersey man one of th
best suspects he had encountered. .

List, meanwhile, has pleaded innocent to the
murder charges and remained in the Union Coun-
ty Jail at Elizabeth, N.J., with bail set at $5 mil

ion. Marranca said List's trial had been tentative:
ly set for December, but no firm date had been
elected. . :
List, an accountant, lived and worked in the
enver area most of the time he was a fugitive.
